summary: Polymorphism means one method call, like student.report(), runs the version that belongs to the object's actual class. A Student variable or array can hold any subclass object.
notes: Student[] roster can hold an HonorsStudent object because HonorsStudent extends Student.
The compiler checks the declared type (Student) to decide which methods you may call. Java picks which version runs when the program runs.
(HonorsStudent) roster[1] is a cast. Casting an object to the wrong class compiles but throws ClassCastException when it runs.
pitfall: Calling roster[1].weightedAverage() fails to compile with "cannot find symbol", even though the object is an HonorsStudent, because the declared type is Student.
